units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Brussels is a city of cafés and small museums, and the weather is changeable.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Carry a light jacket. The center is quite walkable, with cobbled streets and hills, so wear good shoes.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the food everybody talks about?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Belgian beer culture was recognised by UNESCO in 2016.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Chocolate, waffles, and fries are everywhere.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And the praline is traditionally credited to a Brussels chocolatier named Neuhaus, who has a shop in the Galeries.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The streets right around the Grand Place can be crowded and pricey.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Walk two or three streets away and you'll usually find something better.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Then you go indoors, and Brussels is good at that.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The Galeries are covered, there are museums, and a lot of cafés that exist just to give you somewhere to wait the weather out.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: What should I take away from all this?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That Brussels is a city that gets knocked down and rebuilt, and keeps its sense of humour.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A small boy on a fountain in a different costume every week tells you most of it.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Right. Go have a good day.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And if you want the whole story, the long episode will be waiting for you tonight.
